decision.title: Use XML for planning docs going forward
decision.summary: Planning artifacts (plan/summary/roadmap/tasks/decisions/state) must be maintained in XML templates with composable structure.
decision.impact: Improves searchability, allows agents to compose/parse sections, and keeps loop artifacts compact.

decision.title: Loop must ask "what can improve?"
decision.summary: Each phase includes an improvement self-check covering UX, performance, maintenance, and compactness.
decision.impact: Prevents phase drift and encourages refactoring toward smaller, clearer systems.

decision.title: PRD/GRD references are mandatory in each loop
decision.summary: Each phase plan/summary must cite PRD/GRD (or other direction docs) to keep work aligned with overall direction.
decision.impact: Prevents local optimizations from drifting from design intent.

decision.title: Agents must register unique ids before claiming tasks
decision.summary: Each agent generates a unique id and records it in STATE.xml to avoid collisions across concurrent phases.
decision.impact: Improves concurrency safety and makes task ownership discoverable.

decision.title: Planning management via CLI + MCP server
decision.summary: Planning updates and snapshots are managed through a dedicated CLI and MCP server to support multi-agent coordination.
decision.impact: Reduces manual edits and enables automated agent coordination tooling.

decision.title: Ralph Wiggum loop for greenfield overnight automation
decision.summary: Iterative agent loop until a completion promise (e.g. <promise>COMPLETE</promise>) appears in output. Progress persisted via git each iteration; context resets are acceptable. Use for greenfield work: fresh repos, TDD, verifiable tasks. Not for subjective design or production deploys.
decision.impact: Enables unattended overnight runs; pair with git worktrees for parallel greenfield builds. Task spec and promise live in a task file (e.g. RALPH_TASK.md); script runs agent, checks output, commits and repeats until promise or max iterations.

decision.title: Consolidate planning markdown into REQUIREMENTS.xml
decision.summary: Root planning markdown is migrated into `REQUIREMENTS.xml` so XML is the single source.
decision.impact: All root planning data is unified in XML, eliminating duplicate sources.

decision.title: Space Explorer panels require stable IDs and named headers
decision.summary: Interactive Space Explorer panels use explicit `id` / `data-ui-id` attributes and titled headers so future change requests can target exact UI regions.
decision.impact: Improves collaboration speed, reduces ambiguous feedback loops, and keeps visual guidance consistent through context-colored info help controls.

decision.title: Deltas is a primary visualization mode
decision.summary: Space Explorer uses one visualization viewport where `3D`, `JSON`, and `Deltas` all switch the same panel surface; reachability information is represented as compact, icon-coded header badges.
decision.impact: Removes split-panel confusion, increases compactness, and keeps context visible while editing deltas.

decision.title: Space View is the only space selector
decision.summary: `Combined` was promoted into Space View, the separate Content Space selector was removed, and content subsets (`Skill`, `Dialogue`, `Archetype`) became first-class modes using the trait-feature vector path.
decision.impact: Eliminates redundant selection, improves clarity, and keeps nearest/visualization data aligned with the chosen space.

decision.title: Space vectors are feature-assigned per space
decision.summary: Space Explorer now treats each content space as an assigned feature vector (including Fame/Awareness/Guile), with a dedicated Define Feature modal and movement vector feature assignment controls.
decision.impact: Removes static panel ambiguity, supports shared-feature cross-space visualization, and provides an explicit authoring loop for new space features.

decision.title: Active Kael model is always visible from controls
decision.summary: Model Schema Builder now includes a dedicated popup and explicitly displays the active Kael model (`entity.*` inference with base fallback) so schema inspection has clear context.
decision.impact: Reduces ambiguity about which model is being inspected and accelerates schema iteration feedback loops.

decision.title: Model schema selection uses hierarchical tree navigation
decision.summary: The Model Schema popup uses `react-arborist` and groups model IDs by namespace prefix to expose hierarchy (`entity.*`, `item.*`, `room.*`, etc.).
decision.impact: Improves comprehension of schema taxonomy and reduces cognitive load versus a flat list.

decision.title: Named model instances live under model nodes and can be canonical content
decision.summary: Model tree includes instance children (e.g., Kael) under model schemas; instances support canonical toggle and are serialized in patch exports under `contentBindings`.
decision.impact: Clarifies model-vs-instance hierarchy and allows canonical instance bindings to persist as content artifacts.

decision.title: Model viewer interactions use dedicated zustand slice
decision.summary: Model viewer selection/language/tree instance state moved to a dedicated zustand+immer store with shallow selection to avoid full Space Explorer rerenders on tree clicks.
decision.impact: Improves click responsiveness in schema tree and isolates heavy visualization computation from modal interactions.

decision.title: Authoring state persists locally with migration script visibility
decision.summary: Space Explorer UI/model viewer stores persist to browser storage; drag-moving canonical instances between models records migration operations and exposes copyable migration script/code blocks.
decision.impact: Prevents work loss across reloads and makes schema reassignment traceable for code/content migrations.

decision.title: Model schema handoff is file-based with inherited defaults
decision.summary: Model Schema Viewer emits representative TypeScript/C++/C# files across the active inheritance chain and allows per-feature ref default overrides in the same panel.
decision.impact: Improves developer handoff quality by showing concrete file structure, explicit inheritance links, and default values used by canonical assets.

decision.title: Remove ambiguous marker-grouping controls from Space Explorer
decision.summary: 3D marker grouping selector is removed from controls and marker coloring is fixed to branch so the plot behavior is predictable; Space Features removes active-space banner and feature-assign controls.
decision.impact: Reduces UI noise and confusion while keeping direct vector editing focused on current model-space view.

decision.title: Model Space View options derive from active model schema
decision.summary: Space view selection changed from fixed card grid to a dropdown whose options are computed from the active model schema feature-ref spaces, with `(content-combined)` always available.
decision.impact: Keeps exploration controls aligned with model schema definitions and reduces disconnect between schema authoring and runtime space selection.

decision.title: Model selection and creation are centered in schema workflow
decision.summary: Space controls include an explicit model picker from runtime model schemas (same source as model tree), and model tree modal now allows creating new model schemas using current schema as template.
decision.impact: Improves schema authoring flow, keeps selection and creation in one model-centric loop, and avoids hidden/legacy model creation paths.

decision.title: Model tree is the source of model-space selection and multi-model overlays
decision.summary: Controls now defer model selection to the Model Tree workflow, and model nodes include checkboxes for selecting multiple models to overlay in the 3D viewer for the active space.
decision.impact: Unifies model selection UX and enables direct comparison of multiple model spaces without switching context.

decision.title: Feature controls are grouped by inheritance levels
decision.summary: Model Space section controls were removed and feature controls are now grouped by inheritance chain levels (`base`, class layers), while model-space overlays are auto-generated from the same inheritance chain.
decision.impact: Makes base/class composition explicit and avoids duplicate model-space selection controls.

decision.title: Add reusable combatstats inheritance root for entity/item schemas
decision.summary: Runtime schema normalization now injects default stat features and a `combatstats` model, with `entity.base` and `item.base` explicitly extending it through `extendsModelId`, and schema code generation honors explicit inheritance links.
decision.impact: Improves schema reuse and developer handoff by centralizing default combat stats and making inheritance explicit across namespaces.

decision.title: Stat Control is flattened and includes CurrencyStats inheritance
decision.summary: Space Movement controls and merge-inbox panel are removed from the control stack; stat sliders are flattened into Stat Control. Added `currencystats` reusable stat schema and `currency` model extending it so model vectors are expressed as normal stats.
decision.impact: Reduces UI noise and aligns model vectors with a reusable stat-schema inheritance pattern.

decision.title: Pack/report hash binding is explicit and model selection is canonical-first
decision.summary: Space Explorer captures loaded content-pack identity and loaded report binding, displays hash mismatch state, and defaults stat-model selectors to canonical model instances. CI and release workflows emit `play-report-binding` artifacts linked to content-pack report hashes.
decision.impact: Improves traceability between authored content packs and agent playthrough analysis while reducing accidental selection of non-canonical models.

decision.title: Content packs now publish manifest + schema bundle + language stubs
decision.summary: `content-pack.manifest.v1` is generated from bundle space vectors (models/stat classes/canonical assets/spaces), release artifacts include JSON schema bundle and TS/C++/C# model stubs, and play-report API backfills pack binding from current loaded bundle when report metadata is missing.
decision.impact: Aligns Space Explorer authoring with engine/runtime consumption and makes cross-engine handoff deterministic, portable, and traceable by pack hash/version.

decision.title: PRD and requirements: one reusable doc vs many; when to split
decision.summary: Prefer a single REQUIREMENTS.xml (or one requirements “bundle” per product) until scope clearly splits. One doc is fine for: one product, one platform supporting that product, or a small set of related products. Split when: (1) a new product or platform has a distinct stakeholder and release cadence, (2) token/size limits make a single doc unwieldy for context (use planning context tokens to monitor), or (3) teams work in non-overlapping requirement sets. Platform requirements (infra, tooling, MCP, CI) can live in the same doc as product requirements as long as they are clearly sections; when the platform becomes a first-class “product” with its own roadmap, consider a separate PLATFORM-REQUIREMENTS or split REQUIREMENTS by domain. No fixed token cap—use “can we still load and reason about this in one context?” as the signal; when in doubt, split by product/platform boundary rather than by size alone.
decision.impact: Keeps context manageable; avoids premature fragmentation; gives a clear rule for when to create a new requirements doc or restructure (e.g. project → product → platform with multiple products). Planning CLI token report (context tokens) supports monitoring PRD/REQUIREMENTS size.

decision.title: Phase 50 uses Assistant UI + Codex app server with account-linked subscription boundaries
decision.summary: AI integration planning is anchored on Assistant UI for conversation UX and Codex CLI/app server for execution/orchestration paths, while preserving user account/subscription boundaries instead of embedding shared API keys directly in client code.
decision.impact: Implementation tasks must treat auth/session and entitlement checks as first-class architecture concerns, and schema editing flows must run through server-validated endpoints.

decision.title: Use REQUIREMENTS.xml as temporary direction source when REQUIREMENTS.xml is absent
decision.summary: The loop currently points to `.planning/REQUIREMENTS.xml`, but that file is not present; Phase 50 planning uses `.planning/REQUIREMENTS.xml` plus existing roadmap/decisions as authoritative references until a dedicated REQUIREMENTS.xml is restored.
decision.impact: Prevents planning stalls and keeps PRD/GRD citation requirements enforceable with currently available XML sources.

decision.title: Product Owner agent as human stand-in for planning; all agents talk to it
decision.summary: A dedicated “Product Owner” agent is the human stand-in for managing agents and planning: it answers questions, directs work, and updates decisions/requirements. All agents (including Codex CLI / app server agents) can talk to it via MCP or the Codex SDK agent channel. It is implemented and exposed as part of Phase 50 (Assistant UI + Codex app server), so the same integration stack (MCP server, Codex agents) is reused. The Product Owner does not replace human input for major scope changes—it reduces the need for humans to manually read/write planning docs for routine coordination.
decision.impact: Phase 50 deliverables must include an agent role or MCP tooling that can act as this Product Owner; planning-mcp and/or Codex app server agents should be aligned so one agent can fulfill this role. Enables “ask the Product Owner” workflow for any agent.

decision.title: Questions per phase drive decisions and requirements updates
decision.summary: Each phase maintains a set of open questions (in the phase PLAN or a linked questions doc). As questions are answered (by humans or the Product Owner agent), answers are reflected in DECISIONS.xml and REQUIREMENTS.xml so the planning loop stays current. This aligns with Phase 50 and the Product Owner: the PO can own updating questions and propagating answers into decisions/requirements.
decision.impact: Phase plans should include a <questions> section (or equivalent); templates and CLI can support listing/updating phase questions. Keeps planning docs from drifting and gives a single place to “what do we still need to decide?” per phase.

decision.title: Phase 50 executes behind server-controlled feature flags
decision.summary: All new AI integration surfaces (Assistant UI session routing, subscription gating, schema mutation APIs, and report-assisted flows) must ship behind server-controlled flags with explicit cohorts (internal, pilot, general) and kill-switch behavior.
decision.impact: Allows rapid shipping while containing blast radius and supports reversible rollout without reverting code.

decision.title: Phase 50 uses three acceleration lanes with exit criteria
decision.summary: Implementation planning uses lane A (first-party fast path), lane B (hybrid with third-party managed components), and lane C (managed third-party heavy) with explicit switch criteria based on delivery speed, operational risk, and lock-in tolerance.
decision.impact: Keeps delivery velocity high while preserving an intentional build-vs-buy decision and documented fallback path.

decision.title: AI feature flags live in docs-site TOML config files with server-side evaluation
decision.summary: Canonical flag defaults are stored in `docs-site/config/ai-flags.defaults.toml`; optional developer overrides live in `docs-site/config/ai-flags.local.toml` (gitignored) and an optional env-specified TOML path can override both. All evaluation is server-side.
decision.impact: Provides explicit, reviewable defaults while enabling safe local experimentation and emergency overrides without client-side trust.

decision.title: Loop templates include requriements-suggestions block for requirement gap capture
decision.summary: PLAN, SUMMARY, and LOOP templates now include a `requriements-suggestions` section so agents capture requirement gaps and concrete update proposals while continuing execution.
decision.impact: Makes requirement maintenance a built-in loop output and reduces stalls from unresolved documentation gaps.

decision.title: Default acceleration lane is B (hybrid third-party)
decision.summary: Phase 50 closes with lane B as default execution path: keep orchestration and policy boundaries in app server while allowing selected third-party components for delivery speed.
decision.impact: Balances near-term velocity with controllable lock-in and a clear path back to first-party operation.

decision.title: Phase 50 is not complete until Space Explorer chat authoring ships end-to-end
decision.summary: Planning artifacts alone do not satisfy Phase 50. Completion now requires: in-app chat interface in Space Explorer, Codex-backed conversation capable of discussing/editing models/stats/content schema, canonical asset creation, and serialization into content bundle outputs (not schema-only).
decision.impact: Reopens Phase 50 execution tasks and resets DoD to product behavior verification rather than planning closure.

decision.title: Space Explorer chat authoring uses a reusable panel component
decision.summary: Rather than embedding chat logic directly in Space Explorer, Phase 50 implements a reusable `AuthoringChatPanel` component and mounts it in Space Explorer with context payloads. Server route `/api/ai/space-authoring-chat` handles model calls and feature-flag gating.
decision.impact: Keeps heavy Space Explorer iteration manageable and enables reuse of chat authoring in additional surfaces without duplicating state/network logic.

decision.title: Space Explorer chat trigger is a floating Assistant UI modal widget using shadcn controls
decision.summary: Phase 50 chat UX now uses a bottom-right floating widget (`AuthoringAssistantWidget`) with `AssistantModalPrimitive` for open/close and modal positioning, while retaining the reusable `AuthoringChatPanel` as modal content. Inline/embedded chat controls were removed from Space Explorer.
decision.impact: Aligns chat UX with Assistant UI modal patterns, keeps Space Explorer less crowded, and enforces shadcn-first button/input usage for this phase's new UI surface.

decision.title: Space Explorer chat uses structured operations with explicit apply step
decision.summary: Phase 50 chat responses now carry typed operation payloads (models/features/canonical assets/bundle build). The UI shows proposed operations and applies them only on explicit user action, then returns validation/build feedback.
decision.impact: Moves chat from advisory text to safe, auditable authoring mutations while preserving user control and enabling bundle-serialization actions from the same conversation flow.

decision.title: Phase 52 uses encrypted env bundle artifacts for cross-repo secret transport
decision.summary: Docs-site and Unreal plugin secret exchange is standardized on `scripts/env-bundle.mjs` using AES-256-GCM sealed bundles (`.secrets/env.bundle.sealed.json`) with key material provided only from local shell/CI secret stores.
decision.impact: Reduces plaintext-env handling across repos and creates a repeatable, auditable workflow while Supabase distribution and plugin ingestion contracts are being implemented.

decision.title: Use Supabase/S3 for distribution and Dolt for optional patch lineage
decision.summary: Phase 52 delivery architecture uses Supabase Storage (S3-compatible) as the runtime distribution channel for signed downloadable pack artifacts, while Dolt remains an optional local/build-time source for content patch history merged by ingest workflows.
decision.impact: Avoids introducing Dolt as a runtime dependency for Unreal plugin import/download while preserving existing Dolt-backed authoring/version workflows.

decision.title: Split Dolt deep workflow design into dedicated Phase 53
decision.summary: Phase 52 continues with runtime delivery (Supabase publish/pull contracts, Unreal consumption, security, observability), while Dolt governance and promotion policy are explicitly tracked in a new planned Phase 53.
decision.impact: Maintains current delivery momentum and prevents Dolt governance scope from blocking downloadable pack delivery.

decision.title: RepoPlanner package owns all planning API surface; host installs via install-routes
decision.summary: Planning-related API handlers (test-reports/unit, planning-state, planning-cli, etc.) live in vendor/repo-planner/api/. The host Next.js app does not own this logic: it runs install-routes.mjs to write thin re-export route files that delegate to the package. Package can run standalone with REPOPLANNER_PROJECT_ROOT for project-folder selection.
decision.impact: Single source of truth for planning API; host gets updates by re-running install-routes; package is embeddable or standalone.

decision.title: Greenfield vs brownfield for dependency analysis and multi-project cockpit
decision.summary: Greenfield = fresh/new codebases (e.g. reverse-engineering from node_modules to extract feature requirements). Brownfield = existing codebases (normal workflow: analyze usage, assess replaceability). Cockpit can center on any folder that contains .planning (project root); treat each such root as a switchable project so we can work on replacement repos or main repo interchangeably. Projects discovered during existing repo scans (no saved list).
decision.impact: Phase 55 and later: dependency analysis pipeline, requirements in replacement repo REQUIREMENTS.xml, lightweight-rebuild roadmap; project discovery from scans.

decision.title: All planning and tasks use loop XML and planning CLI; no ad-hoc planning docs
decision.summary: Planning, tasks, requirements, roadmap, and decisions use .planning XML documents and the planning CLI workflow. Do not create one-off markdown or standalone planning documents; use REQUIREMENTS.xml, ROADMAP.xml, TASK-REGISTRY.xml, DECISIONS.xml, and phase PLAN/SUMMARY from templates. Replacement repos (e.g. for dependency rebuilds) get the same .planning structure and CLI.
decision.impact: Prevents document drift and keeps a single source of truth; agents and humans follow the same loop; dependency requirements live in replacement repo's REQUIREMENTS.xml (our structure).

decision.title: Cockpit: 5 main tabs with sub-views; semantic color theming and icon usage
decision.summary: Planning cockpit uses 5 main tabs (Overview, Work, State, Tools, Chat) with sub-views where applicable (e.g. Overview = Dashboard | Reports). Second row shows sub-triggers (pills) with icons. All status badges use statusVariant/statusClassName for semantic coloring (done=green, in-progress=amber, failed=red). Icons: one per tab/sub (lucide size-3.5 main, size-3 sub); labels always present. Continue to revisit and refactor layouts for compactness and consistency.
decision.impact: Reduces tab clutter; clear hierarchy; consistent theming and icon usage across cockpit; layouts doc and STYLING.md guide future refactors.

decision.title: Cockpit: phase↔task drill-down, tooltips, motion, icon/color conventions
decision.summary: Phase drill-down: Tasks filterable by phase (click phase in table or in Phases/Questions); Phases tab has “By phase” list with “View tasks (n)”; filter chip with clear when active. Tooltips: native title on metric cards (PlanningMetricCard tooltip prop), section HelpCircle icons with title. Motion: tab content wrapped in motion.div (motion/react) with key=contentKey, fade-in ~150ms. Icons/colors: documented in PLANNING-COCKPIT-REQUIREMENTS 2.10 (LayoutGrid=phases, ListTodo=tasks, HelpCircle=questions, etc.; status via planning-status).
decision.impact: Easier navigation from phase to tasks and back; less wordy UI; consistent transitions and entity visuals.

decision.title: Content authoring cannot rely on model presets or hard-coded spaces lists
decision.summary: Space Explorer and Content Creator must derive authoring shape from the shared schema contract. Hard-coded model presets, fixed feature-name lists, and per-feature spaces arrays are not valid authored schema inputs.
decision.impact: Reopens phase 51 cleanup work: remove preset-driven UI paths, stop baking feature semantics into config, and replace the current permissive content-pack schema surface with an importable JSON Schema-backed contract.

decision.title: Generated content-vector payloads must use neutral vector naming and repo-driven dimensions
decision.summary: Repo-editable schema files define the vector dimensions. Generated and browser-recomputed payloads must not publish traitNames, featureNames, projections.trait, or TypeScript fallback schema defaults.
decision.impact: Space Explorer, space-data generation, and engine vector helpers must read dimensions from the repo schema contract and expose neutral vectorNames/combinedVectorExtensionNames style metadata instead of privileged trait/feature/space naming.

decision.title: Schema-first authoring uses one repo content source document and generated runtime packs
decision.summary: `packages/engine/src/escape-the-dungeon/contracts/source/content-source.json` is the authored root for schema and gameplay contract content. Runtime JSON files under `contracts/data/` are generated from it, content-pack bundles now carry `contentSchema` explicitly, and Kaplay parity uses the generated schema pack rather than TS defaults.
decision.impact: Removes ambiguity about where schema/content should be edited, keeps engine/Kaplay/runtime packs aligned through codegen, and prevents bundle/report consumers from treating `spaceVectors` as the schema definition.

decision.title: Content-pack runtime boundaries must decode typed packs instead of reading raw bundle objects
decision.summary: The current Kaplay/runtime boundary still fetches `content-pack.bundle.v1.json`, parses it, and reads `bundle.packs` as generic objects, only coercing selected pack shapes afterward. Phase 51 remains incomplete until schema-first codegen emits marshal/serializer/code-asset outputs and runtime entrypoints decode typed packs before use. Generated code should come from JSON Schema via quicktype rather than remaining handwritten Zod-only contract code.
decision.impact: Future work must generate codecs/loaders for authored packs and switch Kaplay, engine, and downstream consumers from `unknown`/record access to decoded typed asset graphs. Existing TS/C++/C# model stubs are not sufficient. Unreal `.uasset` files should be created by Unreal editor/import tooling from generated/imported data, not by writing `.uasset` binaries in Node.

decision.title: Keep runtime bundle decode strict and local editor storage loose
decision.summary: Generated `ContentPackBundle` decoding is the runtime boundary for Kaplay, engine, and Space Explorer bundle consumers. Browser-local snapshot state and pending editor/session payloads may stay `unknown` or partial JSON and must be narrowed on read instead of being mislabeled as fully typed records.
decision.impact: Preserves schema-generated runtime correctness without forcing transient browser storage paths to fake strictness, which avoids type drift and keeps partial editor state practical.

decision.title: Human-playable `/play` uses real single-input legends and explicit menu hierarchy
decision.summary: Player-facing labels in Escape the Dungeon must either map to one real key/button or be presented as click/tap actions without implying a shortcut. Multi-character bracket tags like `[ATK]`, `[USE]`, or `[EVO]` are not acceptable as human input guidance, and screen changes must be discoverable through explicit top-level menus and submenus.
decision.impact: Phase 46 work should replace pseudo-shortcut semantics with a stable small legend, readable action names, and a clearer scene hierarchy so `/play` behaves like a game rather than a debug screen router.

decision.title: All gameplay UI is implemented in KAPLAY; host wrappers are delivery-only
decision.summary: Escape the Dungeon does not use React or docs-site as an external gameplay HUD. The game shell, menus, panels, cutscenes, dialogue, combat UI, and input affordances must live inside the KAPLAY application. Docs-site may embed or serve the build, and standalone serving is a preferred iteration path, but that wrapper is not part of the gameplay UI architecture.
decision.impact: Gameplay iteration should happen in `packages/kaplay-demo` scene/layout code. The iframe/docs-shell can remain temporarily for hosting, but UX fixes belong in KAPLAY. Standalone launch is the primary immediate development loop.

decision.title: Combat visuals should be content-authored and codegen-backed, even when the art is temporary
decision.summary: Temporary combat sprites for archetypes, items, and spells are still part of the authored game contract. They now live in `packages/engine/src/escape-the-dungeon/contracts/source/content-source.json`, are validated by the shared schema, flow through quicktype-generated TS/C++/C# contracts, and are consumed by KAPLAY at runtime instead of being hardcoded in a local battle sprite table.
decision.impact: Future combat/UI work can swap placeholder art, add richer visual metadata, or ship content-pack visual updates without touching the KAPLAY runtime wiring. This keeps the game on the schema/codegen path and avoids another drift-prone local content mirror.

decision.title: Spell commands use Generation VIII Sword/Shield type sprites, not full battle portraits
decision.summary: Encounter spell choices should use the compact type-icon family from `MagicbornStudios/sprites` (`sprites/types/generation-viii/sword-shield`, preferably the `small/` variants) instead of reusing full Pokemon battle sprites. The goal is a readable command menu, closer to Pokemon move presentation than party-mon portrait presentation.
decision.impact: KAPLAY combat and rune-forge UI should treat spells as command metadata with compact icon badges. Future spell-slot/loadout work can stay visually consistent without needing oversized portrait art in menus.

decision.title: Gameplay fundamentals stay content-first and Unreal-compatible
decision.summary: Escape the Dungeon is powered by authored content, not scene-local hardcoding. Spell visuals, room-by-room dungeon layouts, encounter triggers, and future tile references must remain in the schema/codegen pipeline so the same payloads can power KAPLAY now and be processed by the Unreal plugin later.
decision.impact: Fast gameplay iteration is still allowed, but new loops should be expressed as authored/generated content wherever possible. This keeps future dungeon tiling, event payloads, and spell-loadout systems aligned with the cross-engine delivery path.

decision.title: Exploration is room-stage first; minimap is supporting context
decision.summary: The center of standalone exploration should present the current room as a playable stage: room description, visible exits, threat/event cue, dialogue/options, and the active spell loadout. Dense ASCII map rendering is secondary context, not the main exploration identity.
decision.impact: Future dungeon-tileset work should preserve room-entry readability and event surfacing. Tile layouts and room art can become richer later, but the gameplay shell should stay oriented around "what is happening in this room now" rather than a pure abstract grid.

decision.title: Prepared spell slots persist in engine state and flow from rune forge to combat
decision.summary: The first spell-slot/pool implementation belongs in the engine snapshot, not only in scene UI. The player now carries prepared spell slots as persisted runtime state, the rune forge edits that loadout, and combat reads it directly to render and resolve spell casting.
decision.impact: This keeps save/load behavior coherent and gives the content pipeline a stable place to attach richer authored spell semantics later. It also avoids a UI-only fake loadout that would diverge from future Unreal/plugin consumers.

decision.title: KAPLAY is the first consumer demo of the content delivery engine
decision.summary: The repo is not just building a game. It is building a schema-first content delivery engine, and the KAPLAY runtime exists as the first playable consumer of generated content contracts before the Unreal delivery pipeline is complete.
decision.impact: Planning and implementation should prioritize traceable content flow, onboarding clarity, and portable contracts. Gameplay work can change presentation quickly, but it should avoid introducing runtime-only content structures that bypass schema/codegen or future Unreal ingestion.

decision.title: Presenter wording must come from authored content contracts, not presenter code
decision.summary: The shared presenter is the single source of action/feed wording, but the wording itself belongs in authored content data. Until `content-source.json` formally carries a presenter-strings pack, the engine runtime may export `contracts/data/presenter-strings.json` directly as a shared contract so KAPLAY and other consumers stop depending on hardcoded presenter literals.
decision.impact: Prevents schema-first drift in player-facing copy, keeps KAPLAY aligned with the content-delivery-engine architecture, and gives later codegen/content-source work a stable target without leaving hardcoded text in `presenter.ts`.

decision.title: Journal and Spellbook may use authored-content marshalling before runtime schemas fully converge
decision.summary: Phase 46 UI surfaces should prefer authored content packs even when the runtime still exposes older or partial structures. Journal can combine authored guide/entity data with runtime quest state, and Spellbook can combine authored spell/category/rarity data with the current runtime skill/loadout system, as long as the bridge is explicit and temporary.
decision.impact: This keeps the playable demo aligned with the gameplay design and content-delivery-engine direction without blocking on full engine/schema convergence. It also makes later cleanup narrower because the display surfaces already consume authored contract data.

decision.title: Stats and Equipped can ship as read-only runtime-plus-content bridges before title persistence lands
decision.summary: Phase 46 may expose `Stats` and `Equipped` as real top-level display screens even though the runtime snapshot does not yet persist a separate equipped-title field. `Stats` should read the current runtime snapshot/status directly, and `Equipped` may combine runtime loadout/archetype data with authored archetype/title metadata as long as the screen clearly remains read-only and does not imply that title equip persistence already exists.
decision.impact: Keeps the top-level gameplay menu set aligned with the gameplay design now, while preserving honesty about the remaining engine-state gap. Later work can add title persistence without throwing away the KAPLAY surfaces.

decision.title: Escape the Dungeon has one canonical play interface, not multiple gameplay modes
decision.summary: The KAPLAY game should expose one coherent play path. Alternate shell concepts like `firstPerson` are not supported gameplay modes anymore and should not appear in scene routing, key legends, or planning language unless a new product decision explicitly reintroduces them.
decision.impact: Prevents UI drift, keeps `/play` aligned with the gameplay design's single navigation/action model, and reduces maintenance overhead from parallel shells that are not part of the game direction.

decision.title: Map is the `M` top-level menu; rune forge remains a context action on `R`
decision.summary: The gameplay shell should reserve `M` for the top-level Map display surface because Map is part of the core global menu set in the gameplay design. Rune forge access remains context-specific and should use `R` when the current room supports it, instead of competing with Map on the same key.
decision.impact: Clarifies menu hierarchy, removes a real key conflict, and keeps room-specific actions separate from persistent display menus.

decision.title: Top-level display menus share one compact archive shell
decision.summary: Journal, Spellbook, Stats, and Equipped should not each reimplement their own list/detail scaffolding inside `grid.ts`. They should share one compact display-screen renderer with common hotkeys, paging, and detail framing, while still allowing authored-content-specific detail views like spell evolution. The shell can lean warmer and more game-facing than the exploration HUD so these menus feel like a codex/archive layer rather than debug panels.
decision.impact: Reduces maintenance risk in the canonical KAPLAY shell, keeps the UI taxonomy aligned with the gameplay design, and makes later extraction of remaining grid-scene logic more incremental. It also gives authored content packs a stable display surface instead of four subtly divergent ones.

decision.title: Rune forge progression bridges authored spell contracts before the full mana and summon systems land
decision.summary: The next convergence step should keep the existing legacy skill runtime alive where needed, but authored spells, runes, rune affinity, spell levels, and authored evolution gates now belong in engine state and the rune forge UI. The forge should read a focused authored spell dossier from runtime state instead of reconstructing progression rules from generic action rows.
decision.impact: This keeps the playable loop aligned with the gameplay design without waiting for the entire mana system or companion/summon runtime. It also narrows later cleanup: once mana and summon systems land, they can replace the temporary bridge behavior without undoing the authored contract flow or the compact forge UI structure.

decision.title: Gameplay HUD and mount traversal belong to the gameplay layer, with mount tuning sourced from content
decision.summary: The canonical KAPLAY shell should distinguish always-on gameplay HUD elements from archive/display screens like Journal or Spellbook. Runtime state such as health, energy, fame, mount status, and current move cost belongs on that HUD. The mount itself should remain content-defined through `mounts.json` and shared contract exports, while whistle is a normal gameplay action and any move-cost benefit should come from the authored mount definition rather than scene-local constants.
decision.impact: Keeps the UI taxonomy aligned with the gameplay design, improves in-play readability without forcing users into top-level menus, and continues the larger rule that designer-tunable/static traversal data should live in content packs while the engine owns only the simulation logic.

decision.title: Combat and bag scene registration should leave `grid.ts` in focused slices, not one giant rewrite
decision.summary: The canonical KAPLAY shell still centers on `grid.ts`, but combat, bag, navigation, and rune-forge scene registration should leave it in small, behavior-preserving slices. Temporary duplicate local copies are acceptable only during the brief extraction transition; once an extracted scene is verified as the live path, the stale local block should be deleted immediately instead of lingering as tolerated debt.
decision.impact: Reduces maintenance risk without forcing a destabilizing one-shot rewrite of the entire shell. It also preserves momentum: each extracted scene becomes a smaller seam for later content-driven UI work, and the follow-up deletion rule keeps `grid.ts` from quietly re-accumulating duplicate ownership.

decision.title: Generic gameplay tunables should move out of `game.ts` into a small shared config pack
decision.summary: Values like prepared spell slot count, default move tick cost, starter loadout spell ids, and generic rune-forge offer cost are designer-tunable rules, not engine dynamics. They should live in a compact shared config contract instead of staying as static constants in `game.ts`, even if more specialized systems like spells or mounts keep their own packs.
decision.impact: Keeps the engine focused on simulation logic, reduces static-data drift between consumers, and gives both KAPLAY and later Unreal/runtime consumers a stable contract for generic gameplay defaults without overloading unrelated packs.

decision.title: Main menu and opening feed must hide pipeline/runtime diagnostics
decision.summary: The KAPLAY start flow is part of the game's fiction, not a developer launcher. Main menu copy and the first seeded gameplay feed should present title, hook, save-state summary, and start actions only. Build/bootstrap/runtime labels like generated content, vector-runtime, parity, or content-pack diagnostics must stay in logs and not appear in player-facing menu or narrative surfaces. Explicit control/device teaching such as keyboard-and-mouse notices also does not belong on the main menu; that guidance belongs in Guides, onboarding, or contextual HUD hints.
decision.impact: Keeps the first impression aligned with the gameplay design, makes the game feel like a product instead of a tool, and separates both internal diagnostics and tutorial housekeeping from player-facing presentation without removing the underlying runtime checks.

decision.title: Dungeon navigation is a floor map with room focus, not an encounter dashboard
decision.summary: The main in-dungeon navigation screen should center on traversing the current floor. It uses a light floor header, the global command panel on the left, room exits/actions on the right, and current-room information in a bottom panel. The old room-log/narrative-feed column and stat-heavy gameplay HUD do not belong on this screen, because they crowd out spatial navigation and make rooms read like fights instead of locations.
decision.impact: Keeps the primary play surface aligned with the gameplay loop, improves readability for gamepad-style menu movement, and makes the room/floor distinction clearer now that the game uses map and sprite visuals instead of text-only panels.

decision.title: Navigation should show only high-level room actions, not tutorial filler or inline dialogue choices
decision.summary: The right-side navigation panel should stay compact and gamepad-friendly. It shows exits plus the high-level actions that belong to the current room. Dialogue choices live behind Talk in the dialogue view, Search should auto-resolve on room entry instead of staying as a standing command, and explanatory copy like marker legends or move-first teaching does not belong on the main play surface.
decision.impact: Reduces on-screen clutter, keeps the floor map readable, and makes the navigation screen feel like traversal rather than a mixed action log, tutorial, and submenu dump.

decision.title: Combat must clearly announce encounter state and keep actors out of the panel lanes
decision.summary: When navigation hands the player into combat, the scene should visibly acknowledge the hostile encounter instead of silently feeling like another panel swap. Combat staging should reserve separate visual lanes for the battle banner, actor sprites, health/status panels, and command/message boxes so enemies do not overlap the player's readout or make the screen feel accidental.
decision.impact: Makes the encounter transition understandable at a glance, improves readability on compact displays, and keeps the combat scene aligned with the same gamepad-friendly hierarchy being established elsewhere in the shell.

decision.title: Dungeon movement should be confirmed from the floor map, not presented as exit rows or a second map mode
decision.summary: The floor map in the main navigation scene is now the primary movement surface. The player highlights an adjacent room on the map, the right-side panel exposes one explicit Move action for that selected destination, and room actions remain separate below it. Exit rows do not belong in the room-action list, empty-result auto-search copy should not interrupt the player, and the older standalone dungeon-map scene should stay collapsed behind the main navigation floor while this movement model is active.
decision.impact: Keeps traversal compact and gamepad-friendly, removes contradictory map experiences, and makes room actions read as room interactions instead of path instructions. It also keeps the screen aligned with the current gameplay-design goal of a map-first dungeon shell.

decision.title: Standalone KAPLAY dev serving should not depend on `npx serve` or a single fixed port
decision.summary: The standalone local iteration path is part of the playable-shell workflow, so it should be robust in the repo itself. The dev runner should use repo-local scripts, not `npx serve`, and it should tolerate the default standalone port already being occupied by selecting the next free local port instead of exiting with a generic failure.
decision.impact: Reduces false-negative local failures during UI iteration, removes one PowerShell-specific `npx` dependency from the inner loop, and makes the KAPLAY standalone workflow more predictable when multiple local servers are already running.

decision.title: KAPLAY should use the loaded content bundle to drive visual asset lookup, not only parity checks
decision.summary: The standalone/game shell already fetches `content-pack.bundle.v1.json`, but if runtime sprite lookup keeps reading static contract imports directly, the live game can drift from the generated bundle even when parity logs look healthy. The loaded bundle should therefore override the active visual lookup tables for the asset groups the bundle already carries, and sprite preload should happen after that override is applied.
decision.impact: Keeps the visible game closer to the generated content bundle, makes asset regressions easier to reason about, and turns the content-pack fetch into a real runtime data path instead of mostly diagnostic metadata. Remaining visual packs that are still outside the bundle schema should be folded into 46-06 contract coverage later.

decision.title: Standalone dev should reject duplicate launches instead of opening more fallback-port sessions
decision.summary: When `dev:standalone` is started twice in the same repo, the result is confusing duplicate watch/build output and multiple local servers drifting across ports like `3004` and `3007`. The local workflow should therefore allow only one active standalone loop per repo and fail fast with a clear message that another process already owns the session.
decision.impact: Turns a confusing “bundle might be broken” symptom into a direct process-level explanation, reduces accidental duplicate watchers, and keeps local debugging focused on real game/runtime issues instead of parallel dev-loop noise.

decision.title: Bundle decode stability depends on source and bundle schemas tracking the real authored pack fields
decision.summary: If a content pack field exists in authored JSON and the runtime bundle but not in the live decode path, KAPLAY can crash before the first scene renders. The immediate example was `itemPack.rarityTiers`, which blanked the UI during content-pack decode. The short-term fix was to remove that unsupported field from the authored item-pack path; the standing rule is that bundle-visible pack fields must either be fully supported in the decode/runtime path or omitted until they are.
decision.impact: Turns a blank-screen boot failure into a concrete contract-maintenance rule: do not leave half-supported authored fields in boot-critical packs. Either wire the field through the full source/schema/generated/runtime path or keep it out of the live bundle. This also reinforces that 46-06 contract coverage is directly tied to playability, not just cleanup.

decision.title: Floor-map directional navigation should prefer valid adjacent rooms over dead directional presses
decision.summary: The dungeon floor is now the primary movement surface, so directional input cannot behave like a brittle exact-match filter. When the player presses a direction that has no direct exit, the selection should snap to the nearest valid adjacent room in a stable fallback order, and the board should still show a clear selected destination. This keeps the map readable and gamepad-friendly.
decision.impact: Prevents the floor map from feeling broken when one cardinal direction is blocked, reduces wasted input, and keeps the right-side Move action synchronized with what the player can actually do from the current room.

decision.title: Discovery fog can hide room detail, but hostile rooms should still punch through with danger borders
decision.summary: The floor map should not flatten into full information by default. Undiscovered rooms should remain shadowed, but rooms containing living hostiles or bosses should still show a visible hostile border so the player can read pressure and route around danger without depending on room-log text.
decision.impact: Keeps the floor readable as a map, preserves discovery tension, and gives the player one clear spatial warning channel for threats without cluttering the action panel or bottom info text.

decision.title: Navigation should separate room actions from global actions
decision.summary: The right panel in the floor-navigation shell should not mix room-specific verbs with global affordances. Room actions belong with the current-room HUD/info block, while the right panel should stay focused on movement and true global actions such as whistle or stream state changes. Undiscovered rooms also should not reveal their type through icons or badges before discovery.
decision.impact: Keeps the navigation shell easier to scan, prevents undiscovered rooms from leaking authored identity too early, and makes the bottom room block the single place where the player reads and acts on the room they currently occupy.

decision.title: Navigation header and room HUD belong inside the same bounded play surface as the floor map
decision.summary: The map-first dungeon screen should read as one game composition. Global commands belong in a compact top header bar inside the navigation frame, not in a separate left command rail or a floor-title banner. The floor board, right-side action column, and current-room HUD should all sit inside the same enclosing navigation frame, with the action lane and bottom room strip reading as parts of the same navigation board as the grid itself. Within that frame, embedded regions should use dividers and seams rather than each drawing their own full bordered card. The current-room strip should also avoid duplicate title/depth copy and should only show verbs that match the room's authored role. Board-state cues must stay distinct: move targets should be subtle, the selected destination should read as a yellow/green target, and hostile rooms should remain dark with red borders and intent arrows instead of bright fills or badges. Cursor movement should update through a lightweight dynamic layer rather than rebuilding the entire shell on every directional input. Top-level display menus like Bag, Journal, Spellbook, Stats, and Equipped should replace only the center viewport as overlays inside this shell instead of routing to separate scene pages.
decision.impact: Gives the navigation shell more visual cohesion, increases usable in-screen space for the floor board, prevents command/navigation chrome from double-framing the screen, stops the room HUD from turning into a separate floating footer, reduces the visual noise from stacked nested borders by keeping the action lane and room strip visually attached to the board, removes misleading room-action clutter, makes movement and hostile pressure legible without resorting to white or overly bright tile fills, keeps destination selection responsive, stops top-level menu use from breaking the continuity of the live dungeon shell, and favors reusable overlay/content modules over continuing to pile more behavior directly into one giant scene file.

decision.title: Canvas UI regressions should be debugged with live button bounds and a reproducible smoke harness
decision.summary: The standalone KAPLAY shell is now command-heavy enough that manual coordinate guessing is not a reliable way to debug broken clicks. The canvas layer should expose a lightweight in-browser debug trail for overlay toggles, selection redraw timings, and button bounds, and the repo should keep a Playwright smoke path that launches the standalone build, clears the intro cutscene, and clicks the live command bar through Bag, Journal, Spellbook, Stats, and Equipped.
decision.impact: Gives us a repeatable way to catch command-bar regressions, turns vague “clicking breaks” reports into concrete event trails, and creates a baseline for later perf work. The traces showed the bottleneck clearly enough to separate fixes: center-overlay opens now avoid full board rerenders, repeated directional selection is below the current debug threshold after keeping the highlight nodes alive, persistent outer-shell layers removed shell teardown cost, and keyed board/action/info tags have brought full room-level navigation renders down to roughly the 115ms range. The remaining drag is now concentrated in the floor-board redraw itself rather than the floor model, runtime lookup path, or menu shell teardown.

decision.title: The standalone shell should return directly to navigation instead of routing through a separate Controls screen
decision.summary: Once Bag, Journal, Spellbook, Stats, and Equipped can live inside the navigation shell, a dedicated `gridActionMenu` / Controls hub becomes dead weight. Escape and back actions should return directly to `gridNavigation`, the old Controls/Explore wording should leave shared command surfaces, and the remaining older full-screen menu scenes should be treated as temporary until they are either overlaid or fully decomposed.
decision.impact: Removes a stale scene hop from the player flow, cuts one source of route confusion while debugging command clicks, and keeps the repo moving toward one coherent in-game shell instead of a mix of old scene pages and newer overlays.

decision.title: Stats should reflect gameplay-design concepts and authored names, not raw engine vectors
decision.summary: The player-facing Stats overlay is not a debugging surface. It should prioritize identity, vitals, progression, narrative traits, gameplay-facing feature signals, and rune affinity using authored names and the gameplay-design vocabulary. Raw runtime diagnostics like feature-vector dumps, fog metrics, semantic-cache counts, or similarly internal readouts should stay out of the Stats screen unless they become explicit gameplay concepts.
decision.impact: Keeps the KAPLAY shell aligned with the gameplay design, makes the menu understandable to players, and narrows future convergence work by pushing the runtime/UI contract toward stable authored labels instead of transient internal metrics.

decision.title: Stats and Equipped should read current identity from runtime status, not local UI heuristics
decision.summary: Once the engine can resolve current title, archetype label, occupation, party role, and mana into player-facing terms, that status payload should be the authoritative UI contract for Stats and Equipped. The overlays can still use authored packs for supporting detail like rarity labels, unlock conditions, and spell metadata, but they should not each re-infer identity separately from archetype guesses or deep engine imports.
decision.impact: Keeps player-facing identity consistent across overlays, reduces duplicated inference logic in KAPLAY UI modules, and moves the repo closer to a stable engine-to-UI contract that can be reused outside the current demo shell.

decision.title: Dialogue content stays a flat authored option list with optional scene grouping
decision.summary: The authored dialogue pack is a flat list of dialogue entries. Entries may carry a `sceneId` for grouping or progression, but the runtime should not expect a second grouped dialogue asset/model. Dialogue evaluation and selection should operate on the flat option list, because that is what the content pack and schemas actually provide.
decision.impact: Prevents another boot-blocking drift between content contracts and the dialogue runtime, keeps the dialogue model aligned with the gameplay design, and removes a misleading internal abstraction that is not part of the authored game language.

decision.title: Next gameplay work should follow contract coverage first, then the core loop pillars
decision.summary: After the menu/HUD shell baseline, the next work order should not default to more UI surfaces. We should first close contract/schema/export drift for the authored packs, then implement the missing player-loop pillars in order: loot/search economy, dungeon tick pressure and boss spawn cadence, authored room-entry interaction/narrative flow, and finally deeper mana/entity-model convergence.
decision.impact: Keeps the implementation sequence aligned with `.planning/GAMEPLAY-DESIGN.xml`, prevents schema-first drift from hiding behind UI work, and makes each next slice compact enough to verify without another large mixed-purpose refactor.

decision.title: Deterministic static content first; no similarity/vector machinery in current phase
decision.summary: Game and demo use only static, authored content: fixed dropdowns and options. No similarity-, distance-, or vector-based selection of actions/events/effects until a later phase that adds narrative-stat-driven options (dialogue first) and eventually emergent narratives. Narrative/progression stats are a named set (see STAT-AND-BEHAVIOUR-TAXONOMY); do not call them vectors or spaces in design or docs.
decision.impact: Prevents reintroducing vector runtime or cosine-similarity APIs; keeps mental model and implementation stable for the current game. Later phase can add narrative stats for option gating and similarity/distance for emergent narratives on top of this base.

decision.title: Navigation board performance should preserve room tiles and redraw only state decorations
decision.summary: The floor map should not recreate every room tile shadow and base cell on each room refresh. The stable board geometry belongs on a persistent base layer, while discovery fills, current-room emphasis, hostile borders, intent arrows, badges, and the player marker belong on a lighter decoration layer that can be redrawn independently.
decision.impact: Reduces room-refresh churn in the KAPLAY shell, keeps movement and overlay work off the heavy full-tile path, and makes the remaining navigation lag easier to isolate to board decorations instead of shell teardown or room-layout reconstruction.

decision.title: Navigation side and bottom panels should keep their text blocks mounted
decision.summary: The action rail and current-room HUD should not redraw their section labels, room title, room feature, and body lines every time the room state changes. Those text nodes should stay mounted and update in place, while only action-button groups rerender when the actionable list changes.
decision.impact: Pushes more of the navigation shell onto the property-update path, narrows panel churn to button rebuilds instead of full text relayout, and leaves the remaining performance work focused on decorations and button/button-registry overhead.

decision.title: Navigation action lists should use bounded visible slots with a More overflow overlay
decision.summary: The live navigation shell should not try to show every room or global action inline when action counts spike. The primary shell should keep a small visible slot budget for room actions and global actions, and route overflow through a center-overlay `More` list so the interaction model stays compact and gamepad-friendly.
decision.impact: Keeps the navigation UI readable under variable action counts, avoids chasing a fully unbounded inline button layout, and gives the performance work a stable bounded target for persistent button slots instead of a constantly resizing list region.

decision.title: Navigation should keep bounded action slots and board decorations mounted between room updates
decision.summary: Once navigation action lists are bounded, their visible button slots should stay mounted and update label, tone, visibility, and callback target in place. The same rule applies to board-decoration nodes like hostile borders, selected-room emphasis, and intent arrows: room-state updates should mutate the existing nodes instead of rebuilding those regions wholesale.
decision.impact: Closes the last obvious structural performance sink in the navigation shell, narrows room refresh cost to property updates instead of node churn, and leaves any remaining lag attributable to the underlying canvas/runtime path rather than repeated UI reconstruction.

decision.title: Map menu shows world map by default; zoom in to current dungeon floor
decision.summary: Two distinct map levels: (1) World map = all regions (overworld hubs, dungeon-floors region, transitions). Dungeons are scoped to a region (e.g. wilderness or outskirts). (2) Floor map = single depth room grid. The Map menu opens on the world map by default; the player zooms in to see the current dungeon floor (floor map). This avoids confusion where "[M] Map" currently shows only the floor grid with no regional context.
decision.impact: Clarifies product intent for maps: world map first, then zoom to floor. Implementation work: expose world map pack in engine/runtime, add world map view in KAPLAY, and make [M] Map open world map with zoom-in to floor.

decision.title: Generated MDX frontmatter should quote package-name strings
decision.summary: The docs generator emits YAML frontmatter, so values containing special characters like `@dungeonbreak/engine` must be quoted instead of written as bare strings. Generated docs should produce valid frontmatter directly, not rely on manual patching of individual MDX files after generation.
decision.impact: Prevents the docs site from failing at parse time on generated API pages, keeps `docs:generate` idempotent, and makes the Next docs build fail on real compilation issues instead of malformed frontmatter.

decision.title: Turn worker should sync state once, then dispatch actions against the synced engine
decision.summary: The KAPLAY runtime should not post the full engine snapshot with every player action when worker turns are enabled. The worker first receives a sync request with seed plus snapshot, restores the deterministic engine, and then accepts action-only dispatch messages until state changes require a resync.
decision.impact: Keeps the core engine deterministic and synchronous while moving UI-side turn resolution off the main thread, reduces payload churn per turn, and creates a stable boundary for timing/debug events around queued, resolved, rejected, and failed turns.

decision.title: Boss room should stay visibly revealed on the navigation board
decision.summary: The floor objective should not hide behind the same discovery rules as ordinary rooms. Boss rooms stay visibly revealed, publish the crown-first tile icon language, and can show boss presence like a discovered board piece even before player entry.
decision.impact: Makes the route objective legible at a glance, supports the new full-cell board language, and keeps navigation planning readable without requiring extra HUD text or debug overlays.

decision.title: Gameplay feed should use actor-aware MMO-style prefixes
decision.summary: Livestream and dungeon events should share one readable feed vocabulary instead of raw engine strings. System, player, boss, dungeoneer, live, combat, and related channels should format with stable prefixes and room context so humans and tests can skim what happened immediately.
decision.impact: Turns the gameplay feed into part of the readability pass, improves reviewability in smoke tests and debug tooling, and avoids a split between livestream narration and dungeon event reporting.

decision.title: Existing initiative meters are the active speed-queue model
decision.summary: Queue work should extend the engine's current initiative-meter fields (`initiativeMeters`, `lastInitiativeOrder`, surfaced `initiativeQueue`) rather than introducing a second scheduling abstraction beside them. Agility-driven gain, ready thresholds, and ordered ready actors are now the live queue contract for autonomous actors.
decision.impact: Keeps speed/queue behavior deterministic, aligns docs with runtime reality, and lets workerization/perf work measure and optimize the real queue path instead of a hypothetical future replacement.

decision.title: Playable-loop turn performance should use explicit budgets
decision.summary: The active phase should treat the package-local perf harness as a real guardrail: average turn resolution <= 700ms, p95 <= 1200ms, and max <= 1600ms across the deterministic move-run sample unless we intentionally re-baseline those thresholds.
decision.impact: Prevents “performance” from staying qualitative, keeps worker and queue changes tied to measurable outcomes, and gives gameplay review a concrete regression signal alongside smoke tests and debug traces.

decision.title: Board and room-panel presence sprites should share one priority order
decision.summary: Presence presentation should resolve from one deterministic order across board cells, hover details, and room portraits: boss first, then hostile, then dungeoneer, then room emblem fallback. Authored media layers onto this order; it does not replace the shared fallback logic with per-screen exceptions.
decision.impact: Keeps room identity consistent across views, makes small-scale board sprites more readable, and gives future authored media a stable placement rule instead of ad hoc panel-specific logic.

decision.title: Combat rooms are removed in favor of room-focus scenes plus encounter transitions
decision.summary: Combat should only start from encounter presence, not from a dedicated room-feature taxonomy. Treasure, training, and rune forge now use a room-focus navigation mode with concrete room actions, scene art, boss-aware board presence, and numeric/keycap affordances while the grid remains a toggleable sibling view.
decision.impact: Removes contradictory room semantics, makes authored non-combat rooms feel actionable, keeps the board shell consistent with encounters, and prevents the UI from regressing back to bracketed pseudo-hotkey labels or empty treasure/training panels.

decision.title: Loadout menus keep context actions at the top with icon-first filters and rarity cues
decision.summary: Bag and spellbook overlays should treat selection clarity as part of gameplay readability, not as a footer-only convenience. The active selection now owns a top-pinned action strip, filters and sort controls stay icon-first, arrow-selection hints remain visible in the menu header area, and item/spell rarity is expressed through shared icon and color treatment.
decision.impact: Preparation and equipment changes are easier to parse during play, selected pool/inventory cards read more decisively, and the menu shell stays aligned with the broader board/readability work instead of drifting back toward debug-like text lists.

decision.title: Navigation footer becomes a live gameplay feed with explicit keycaps
decision.summary: The lower navigation panel should show player-facing gameplay events only: system, live, player, boss, dungeoneer, and entity updates. Room-focus tabs and navigation actions should use stable keyboard-style affordances (`M`, `R`, `V`, `X`, `Space`), and hidden actions must not leave shadow bars or hint clutter behind.
decision.impact: This keeps the shell readable during play, removes debug-like leftover surfaces, and aligns the room-focus/navigation UX with the gameplay-design requirement for a shared live feed and compact explicit controls.
